ground.name: Bladder wrack
ground.source: underwater — Fucus vesiculosus, North Atlantic and Baltic intertidal to shallow subtidal rock, olive-brown rockweed 30-100 cm — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Fucus vesiculosus, North Atlantic and Baltic intertidal to shallow subtidal rock, olive-brown rockweed 30-1
traits.leaf_shape: strap or rosette leaves in a clump on a branch
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: brown alga: flat dichotomous fronds with a midrib and paired air bladders, drawn as straps

bark.note: holdfast and short stipe; no stem surface

ground.silhouette: olive-brown forked straps draped over rock at low tide

growth.juvenile_note: No juvenile form to draw: zygotes stick to rock and within weeks become tiny flat germlings anchored by a disc; the young frond is a small, flat, forked olive blade with a midrib that gains paired air bladders as it grows. Mature plants are 30-100 cm leathery forked fronds with paired bladders and swollen, warty fruiting tips.
growth.source: MarLIN species account (Fucus vesiculosus: germlings visible in ~2 weeks; growth 0.3-0.8 cm/week in summer; lifespan 2-5 yr; receptacles form in winter, gametes mid-winter to late summer); Wikipedia (fronds to 150 x 2.5 cm with midrib and paired vesicles; sheltered mid-lower shores).

ground.name: Sea lettuce
ground.source: underwater — Ulva lactuca, worldwide shallow shelf rock and pools, bright-green sheets 10-30 cm — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Ulva lactuca, worldwide shallow shelf rock and pools, bright-green sheets 10-30 cm — Wikipedia
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: green alga: thin translucent bright green sheets

ground.silhouette: bright green translucent sheets on rock and mud

growth.juvenile_note: Settled swimming spores or zygotes (microscopic) grow into a short green filament, then a tiny tube or cushion that splits open into a flat blade only two cells thick on a minute disc holdfast. It shows as a bright green fleck after 1-2 weeks and expands in a few weeks into a crinkled, translucent, lettuce-like sheet; fertile margins turn olive-yellow, release spores and then fall apart.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ulva lactuca): sheet to 18 cm or more long and up to 30 cm across, on rocks and other algae in the littoral and sublittoral worldwide; diploid and haploid plants look alike, alternating via zoospores and gametes; eaten in soups and salads. Settlement-to-visible, growth and fertility timings estimated from the genus (fast-growing, fertile within weeks, repeated summer spore releases).

bark.note: fleshy sprawling green stems, often purple-tinged

ground.silhouette: sprawling fleshy mound of lobed leaves, lilac flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Big seeds in corky, floating pod segments sprout in the drift line (in spring on Atlantic coasts, after autumn rains in the Mediterranean). Two thick, fleshy, kidney-shaped cotyledons, then glossy, succulent, blue-green, deeply lobed leaves; it branches from the base into a sprawling, bushy clump that flowers pale lilac within about two months.
growth.source: Wikipedia (annual, 15-45 cm, flowers Jun-Aug in the UK, white to lilac 4-petalled flowers to 2.5 cm, corky 1-3 cm fruits float); Davy et al. 2006 Biological Flora of the British Isles (spring germination in the north, autumn in the Mediterranean); timings estimated.

ground.origin: North Atlantic and North Pacific coasts

traits.trunk: long woody or soft climbing stem on a host
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: brown alga: single undivided blade with ruffled margins on a short stipe

bark.note: holdfast and short stipe; no stem surface

ground.silhouette: single long ruffled brown blade swaying from a stipe

growth.juvenile_note: No seedling: spores grow into microscopic threads (gametophytes) and each fertilised egg grows into a tiny flat blade on a short stalk with a small claw-like holdfast. Young blades are thin, smooth and golden-brown; adults are one long undivided blade (1-5 m) with ruffled, wavy edges and a puckered centre, growing from the base while the tip wears away.
growth.source: Luning 1990, Seaweeds (Laminariales life cycle, spring growth peak, sori in autumn-winter); Bartsch et al. 2008 Eur J Phycol (Laminaria s.l. review: sporophytes live 2-4+ yr); kelp farming practice (seeded Oct-Nov, 1-3 m by Apr-May); Wikipedia (to 5 m x 20 cm)

fruiting.source: A kelp has no flowers or fruit. Mapped: 'flower' = the dark sorus patch that forms on the mid-blade in autumn-winter (Luning 1990; Bartsch et al. 2008); 'pollinator' = water carrying zoospores and sperm; 'fruit' = the ripe sorus, which releases spores and then sloughs off; the blade itself is eaten raw or cooked.
